## Critique
- claim-1: Validated project context distinguishes the 2011 minimality conjecture from the stronger integral quotient statement. It does not provide the required 2024 full-text theorem certificate.
- claim-2: The abstract establishes only that the authors claim to prove “the minimality conjecture.” It does not identify the exact theorem, coefficient ring, parameter hypotheses, ideals, or generating families, so applicability to the current \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is unverified.
- claim-3: Correct only after explicitly invoking that the specified \(N\)-element families already generate \(J\). Then every generating family surjects onto \(J/\Lambda_+J\), while \(\mathbb Z^N\) needs at least \(N\) generators. The converse fails: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(A_+=(x)\), and \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the displayed pair is minimal but
  \[
  J/A_+J\cong \mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2,
  \]
  not \(\mathbb Z^2\).
- claim-4: Correct and fatal to acceptance. Provider search ran, but no bounded 2024 full-text theorem passage with stable locators was supplied. Therefore the requested source-refresh target was **not established**. The abstract-level adjacent result cannot substitute for it.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Prove the implication using the known generation of the two \(N\)-element families, and include the explicit graded counterexample \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(J=(2x,x^2)\) showing that minimality does not imply free integral indecomposables.
- [source-refresh] Retrieve from versioned arXiv full text `2209.02011v2` or the DOI version a bounded passage containing the exact theorem statement, its hypotheses and coefficient ring, together with bounded definition passages identifying the relevant \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), parameters \(a,b\), and the two generating families; cite stable theorem/page/equation or versioned line locators.

## Required revisions
- Replace the abstract-only discussion with the required full-text excerpts and a line-by-line applicability check.
- State separately whether the 2024 theorem proves minimality and whether it proves
  \[
  J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}
  \cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}.
  \]
- Do not infer the stronger integral statement unless the retrieved theorem explicitly establishes torsion-freeness, rank, and the basis images.
